slice: C3: block-local repeated integer extension selection
observed: Lowerer::zero_extend and sign_extend create fresh native temporaries for each request. They do not reuse an identical same-source extension already selected in that block. Existing C2 combines only adjacent single-use emission idioms and remains unadmitted after its compile-bound miss. N01 recorded 4,132 excess extension/mask bytes across the library TUs; that is a prioritization ceiling, not predicted C3 gain. Existing comparison-to-branch and compared-value CSEL selection already exist and are not new work.

scope.included: After ordinary MIR lowering and before SSA destruction/allocation, optionally reuse an earlier identical integer extension result within the same block. Three bounded pattern families: Extend's existing signed/unsigned byte/half/word forms; Bfx with lsb=0 and a proper sub-register width; BinaryImm AND with a nonzero low contiguous mask narrower than its register. Keys retain opcode, sign, source identity/class, destination class, width and mask/extract size. Only unique definitions and local non-edge uses can be removed. Replace uses of the removed destination directly by the retained result. No algebraic identity, range reasoning or change of width is inferred.
scope.boundaries: Reset available expressions at block boundaries and every non-discardable instruction, including calls, asm, memory and strict fenv. Preserve ordered flags producer/consumer adjacency. Source and result definitions must be unique; multiple definitions, cross-block destination uses, edge transport and class/operation differences prevent reuse. No physical-register reuse assumption or hidden cross-block cache.
scope.unchanged: All EvoIR, MIR opcode meanings, interpreters, effect/UB rules, certificates, registries, ABI, allocator and independent allocation verifier. No guard folding, generic CSE/GVN, extension composition, mask strengthening, instruction speculation or new opcode.
scope.default: OFF. Existing protected-profile suppression remains. C2 stays excluded from measured admitted cumulative options.
scope.placement: Target-specific bounded selector under isa/aarch64, using the existing operand facts. Extend targets/aarch64/patterns and its existing generator with explicit C3 rows; no generic opcode language, new registry or new audit layer.

interface.driver: Add extensions to the duplicate-free --isel-opt list. Canonical order constants,local,extensions; all old names and OFF output unchanged. Exact IR adapter and native corpus hook use the same parser. Reject empty, unknown, duplicate, repeated and --check combinations.
interface.telemetry: Reuse the existing producer-only native selection-count comments and S1/N01 measurements. Report selected/rejected pattern counts and actual bytes separately; no certificate credit.
interface.spec: EvoMIR implementation-policy revision describing repeated selection reuse only, not a new instruction or semantic contract. New patterns receive explicit finite-validation/no-SMT-proof dispositions because N07 E3's pinned generator limitation remains.

red: Public C/IR path showing an actually repeated extension after lowering; OFF preserves it, ON reuses it. If the proposed opportunity does not materialize, freeze a negative preflight instead of expanding scope.

Existing MIR interpreter and EvoIR comparison for each admitted extension family, W/X widths, signed/unsigned extrema, odd-width masks and full-register boundaries; allocation verifier remains unchanged.
Distinct signedness, widths, masks, source identities/classes, multiple definitions, nonlocal/edge uses, calls, asm, loads/stores and strict-FP barriers retain necessary computations.
Flags adjacency and selected terminator operands remain valid; long duplicate sequences use direct representatives rather than a bounded alias chase.
Default byte identity, protected profiles, malformed option lists, all admitted combinations, public native tests and exact IR adapter.

acceptance.native: 384 Darwin and 384 sealed Linux cases OFF/ON, serial; object twins equal, OFF bytes match T3, actual execution agrees. Focused native references exercise each admitted family and fence/width negatives.
acceptance.six_units: Freeze six A/B plans before measurement: fresh OFF, extensions-only, and cumulative frame+C1+copy+reload+extensions. Both UB profiles, three compile observations and two object builds; current T3 OFF baselines retained. Original selected-TU harnesses and independent chain replay with zero completed rejection/bundle failure. No resampling to improve a result.

bounds.comparison: Each new arm versus matched fresh OFF; report incremental cumulative size versus T3 separately.

acceptance.coverage: N02 stays 70 admitted inputs / 187 opaque; legacy integer-mix 1001/1002 source-event mismatch NOT_VALIDATED. No full applications, kernel, latency, default admission or B1/B6 proof inferred.
acceptance.stop: One bounded implementation and frozen cohort. Preserve zero/negative results and cost misses; decline an unsafe pattern rather than broaden it. Remaining conditional-compare or control restructuring requiring new MIR semantics is outside this slice and receives an explicit unimplemented disposition, not speculative new instructions.

resources.retention: Only compact receipts, category summaries and minimal reproducers. Retire completed owned objects after hash/handle checks while preserving a current OFF and cumulative baseline. No raw captures in Git, new target/workspace/kernel tree or VM disk.

claim_ceiling: Opt-in repeated integer extension selection with finite MIR/native validation, not universal instruction correctness, verified EqSat benefit, default admission, complete instruction selection or the 1.4 product target.
